title: s(18) = (7+√7)/2: Mira Cult's computer-assisted optimality proof (pointer, to import and review)

body:
This tracks an external optimality claim at n = 18 that the record does not yet hold. It was opened by the maintainer's intake from a public post; it is not a registration request from the author.

**Source.**

- Post: Mira (@_Mira___Mira_) on X, 2026-11-20 03:06:47Z: "Astra 6.2 has a proof this is the best way to pack 18 unit squares into a square." (https://x.com/_mira___mira_/status/2123614000382669312)
- Repository: https://github.com/Mira-Cult/math/blob/main/notes/geometry/unit-square-packing-18/README.md. The head was `78bec6aacebf304d942a9225e16c2f18165778ff` when read on 2026-11-20.

**Claim, in the source's words.** "For eighteen squares, the optimum is s(18) = (7+√7)/2 = 4.822875655286…". The note calls this "an exact, computer-assisted optimality proof". Hämäläinen's earlier packing already attains this side. The contribution is the matching lower bound "with no restriction on the orientations or contact pattern". The note says the theorem fixes the optimal side; it does not classify all the configurations that attain it.

**How the source says the proof works.**

- **Construction:** an exact construction (`replay/six-tilt18.json`) with twelve axis-parallel squares and six tilted ones, coordinates in Q(√7), and an exact checker (`replay/six_tilt18.py`).
- **Lower bound:**
  - 21 points in a slightly larger rational test box give every tile an interior point.
  - Up to the box's eight symmetries, that leaves 187 assignments of occupied marks.
  - 181 cases are refuted outright by exact bounds.
  - In the other six, branches that contain an optimal configuration are shown to force the actual enclosing side to be at least the claimed optimum.
- **Files:** the proof is in `proof.md`, the certificate map and replay commands in `replay/README.md`, and verification and references in `verification.md`.
- **AI assistance:** the source states that GPT-6.2 Astra developed the lower bound and the construction under Mira Cult's direction, and that a separate OpenAI model review checked the assembly and reran the seven certificate groups.

**Where the record stands at 18.** The case is open (`packing/frontier/n-018.md`), with conjectured optimum 4.82287565553229, which is (7+√7)/2. If the claim holds, it would settle n = 18.

**What intake owes.** Per `packing/campaign/result-import.md`:

1. Enter this in `result-requests.yaml` with an import bead, and add the repository to the watch list.
2. Retain the source at a pinned revision, with its digests.
3. Replay the construction exactly. Rerun every certificate group the replay README names, using the source's own commands and, where the record has them, maintained routes.
4. Run a blind stage 4 mathematical review of the lower-bound argument. This is an optimality claim, so the review must cover:
   - the covering lemma (21 points, every tile gets one);
   - the completeness of the 187 cases under the symmetry reduction;
   - the soundness of the exact bounds;
   - the six tight cases.
5. Register at the rungs the evidence supports, and update n = 18's lower bound and status only as far as the reviewed evidence goes.
6. Reply to the author, inviting a registration request here if they want one.

Context: Mira's earlier computer-assisted lower bound at n = 17 (the 4.613 certificate) was reviewed in `docs/project/reviews/review-2026-09-20-n17-r012-and-mira-4613-proof-review.md`.
